findings.claim: The mapError method checks for a nonFieldErrors payload before calling mapBannedSafeError, so a response that is both a 451 and contains a nonFieldErrors array would never reach the banned-Safe rewrite; reordering to check the banned-Safe case first would make the logic robust to this upstream payload shape even though it is unlikely under the current contract.

The same status-excluding helper loop (looping faker.internet.httpStatusCode until it isn't UNAVAILABLE_FOR_LEGAL_REASONS_STATUS) is duplicated across three spec files instead of being extracted into a shared test utility such as src/__tests__/faker.ts, which would remove duplication and centralize future exclusions.

The new integration test covers the /balances/usd route for the banned-Safe path but does not add a mirrored test for /collectibles, even though both getBalances and getCollectibles now apply mapBannedSafeError in SafeBalancesApi, so route-level wiring for the second catch site is only verified at the datasource level, not the integration level.

The helper is named mapBannedSafeError after the specific upstream cause (banned Safe) rather than after its actual behavior of rewriting any 451 response payload into a message field that HttpErrorFactory can read, so if another upstream later returns 451 for a different reason, the name would be misleading; a name like map451ResponsePayload would better reflect its function.
